'''Véronique Gouverneur''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 8 November 1964 in [[Geel|Geel, Belgium]]) is a Belgian-British chemist. She is the [[Waynflete Professor of Chemistry]] at [[Magdalen College, Oxford|Magdalen College]] at the [[University of Oxford]] in the United Kingdom.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name=epmc>{{EuropePMC|ORCID=0000-0001-8638-5308}}</ref> Prior to the Waynflete professorship, she held a tutorial fellowship at [[Merton College, Oxford]].<ref name="WIC">{{cite journal|last1=Köster|first1=Vera|year=2011|title=Women in Chemistry – Interview with Veronique Gouverneur|journal=ChemViews|doi=10.1002/chemv.201000094}}</ref> Her research on [[Organofluorine chemistry|fluorine chemistry]] has received many professional and scholarly awards.<ref name="chemworld" /> She was elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>{{cite web | title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members – NAS | url=https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/ }}</ref>

== Education ==
Gouverneur obtained her undergraduate degree (a master's degree in chemistry),<ref name="chemie" /> and then in 1991 her [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctorate]], from the [[Université catholique de Louvain]].<ref name="WIC" /> She moved in 1992 to the [[Scripps Research Institute]] in the US, returning to Europe in 1994.<ref name="WIC" /> She accepted a position of [[Academic ranks in France|Maître de Conférence]] at [[Louis Pasteur University]], working with [[Charles Mioskowski]] and was associate member of the [[Institut de Science et d'Ingénierie Supramoléculaires]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Veronique Gouverneur|url=http://gouverneur.chem.ox.ac.uk/veronique.aspx|access-date=7 March 2020|website=Oxford Chemistry}}</ref>  

==Career and research==
She joined the department of chemistry at Oxford in 1998, becoming [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]] in 2006<ref name="chem.uzh.ch">{{Cite web|title=Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin Symposium 2012: Biography|url=http://www.chem.uzh.ch/static/events/dch/2012/Gouverneur.html|access-date=18 November 2015|website=chem.uzh.ch|archive-date=19 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119141135/http://www.chem.uzh.ch/static/events/dch/2012/Gouverneur.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and professor in 2008.<ref name="WIC" /> In her research career, she chose fluorine chemistry as a distinctive area to focus on because fluorine compounds have many applications, including in [[pharmaceutical drug]]s and in [[positron emission tomography]] (PET) scans.<ref name="chemworld">{{cite journal|last1=Cote|first1=Marie|title=Following her passion|journal=Chemistry World|date=11 January 2013|url=http://www.rsc.org/chemistryworld/2013/01/interview-veronique-gouverneur|access-date=18 November 2015|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> She has also had [[Visiting scholar|visiting professor]] posts at the [[University of Paris-X|University of Paris X]] and the Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Awards and Honours|url = http://users.ox.ac.uk/~vgweb/veroniqueawards.html|website = Gouverneur group web site, University of Oxford|access-date = 18 November 2015|archive-date = 26 March 2018|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180326083420/http://users.ox.ac.uk/~vgweb/veroniqueawards.html|url-status = dead}}</ref> In 2022, she was appointed as the [[Waynflete Professor of Chemistry]], a post that dates back to 1865.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 October 2022 |title=Véronique Gouverneur appointed Waynflete Professor of Chemistry |url=https://www.chem.ox.ac.uk/article/veronique-gouverneur-appointed-waynflete-professor-of-chemistry |access-date=2 November 2022 |website=www.chem.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Merton College, Oxford-2022">{{Cite web |date=21 October 2022 |title=Véronique Gouverneur appointed as Waynflete Professor of Chemistry |url=https://www.merton.ox.ac.uk/news/veronique-gouverneur-appointed-waynflete-professor-chemistry |access-date=2 November 2022 |website=Merton College, Oxford |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
Gouverneur won the [[AstraZeneca]] Research Award for [[organic chemistry]] in 2005.<ref name="chem.uzh.ch" /> She was the 2008 winner of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (RSC) [[Bader Award]], "for her important contributions to synthetic organofluorine chemistry."<ref>{{cite web|publisher=rsc.org|title=Bader Award 2008 winner|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/BaderAward/2008winner.asp|access-date=18 November 2015}}</ref> In 2010, she was elected Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fellow (FRSC)|url=https://www.rsc.org/membership-and-community/join/fellow/|access-date=20 February 2021|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|date=24 August 2017 |language=en-GB}}</ref> and received the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry|IUPAC]] Distinguished Woman in Chemistry Award.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=11 November 2011|title=2011 IUPAC Awards to Distinguished Women in Chemistry and Chemical Engineering|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/anie.201106196|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|language=en|volume=50|issue=46|pages=10763–10764|doi=10.1002/anie.201106196|bibcode=2011ACIE...5010763. |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2011 she was awarded the Liebig Lectureship Award of the Organic Division of the German Chemical Society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Liebig-Lectureship {{!}} Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker e.V.|url=https://www.gdch.de/netzwerk-strukturen/fachstrukturen/liebig-vereinigung-fuer-organische-chemie/liebig-lectureship.html|access-date=20 February 2021|website=www.gdch.de|language=de}}</ref> In 2012, she was holding the [[Blaise Pascal Chair]] (ENS/CEA, France).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winners 2012 – Chaires Blaise Pascal|url=http://www.chaires-blaise-pascal.ens.fr/laureats/laureats-2012/?lang=en|access-date=20 February 2021|website=www.chaires-blaise-pascal.ens.fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Andres|first=Jeanne Therese|date=3 February 2016|title=Véronique Gouverneur – our new ChemComm Chair – Chemical Communications Blog|url=https://blogs.rsc.org/cc/2016/02/03/veronique-gouverneur-new-chemcomm-chair/|access-date=20 February 2021|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2013, the UK's [[Royal Society]] selected her as one of 27 [[Royal Society Wolfson Fellowship|Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]] holders.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Royal Society announces new round of Wolfson Research Merit Awards|url = https://royalsociety.org/news/2013/new-wolfson-research-merit-awards/|publisher = royalsociety.org|access-date = 18 November 2015}}</ref> In 2015, Gouverneur received the [[American Chemical Society]] Award for Creative Work in Fluorine Chemistry "for her contribution to late-stage fluorination and for invigorating creatively the field of [<sup>18</sup>F] radiochemistry for applications in Positron Emission Tomography."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/recipients/2015-national-award-recipients.html|publisher=acs.org|title=2015 National Award Recipients|access-date=18 November 2015}}</ref> In 2016, she was an International Visiting Research Scholar of the [[Peter Wall Institute for Advanced Studies]] ([[University of British Columbia]])<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 September 2016|title=Véronique Gouverneur|url=https://pwias.ubc.ca/profile/veronique-gouverneur|access-date=20 February 2021|website=Peter Wall Institute for Advanced Studies}}</ref> and held the Tetrahedron Chair at the Belgian Organic Synthesis Symposium (BOSS) meeting.<ref>{{Cite web|title=BOSS XVII – Tetrahedron Chair|url=https://www.boss-symposium.org/tetrahedron-chair|access-date=20 February 2021|website=www.boss-symposium.org}}</ref> That year, she received the RSC [[Tilden Prize]] for her interdisciplinary work in the area of organofluorine chemistry and radiochemistry, and the impact of her discoveries in medicine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Previous winners|url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/find-a-prize/tilden-prizes/previous-winners/|access-date=20 February 2021|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Royal Society of Chemistry Prizes and Awards 2016|url=https://www.rsc.org/news-events/articles/2016/may/awards-and-prizes-2016/|access-date=20 February 2021|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|date=9 May 2016 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 2017, Gouverneur become an elected member of the European Academy of Sciences (EURASC).<ref>{{Cite web|title=European Academy of Sciences – Véronique Gouverneur|url=https://www.eurasc.org/user/278/veronique-gouverneur|access-date=20 February 2021|website=www.eurasc.org}}</ref> She received a [[European Research Council]] Advanced Grant in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|date=27 March 2019|title=ERC Advanced Grants 2018 – All domains by country|url=https://erc.europa.eu/content/erc-advanced-grants-2018-all-domains-country|access-date=20 February 2021|website=ERC: European Research Council|language=en}}</ref> In 2019, she received the RSC [[Organic Stereochemistry Award]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=USW presents the RSC's 2019–20 Award Winners' Lecture Tour – Organic Stereochemistry Award Winner : Professor Véronique Gouverneur|url=https://www.rsc.org/events/detail/42657/usw-presents-the-rscs-2019-20-award-winners-lecture-tour-organic-stereochemistry-award-winner-professor-v-ronique-gouverneur|access-date=20 February 2021|website=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> and the Prelog Medal ([[ETH Zurich|ETH]]).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Past Prelog-Lecturers and Their Laudations|url=https://chab.ethz.ch/en/research/institutes/LOC/prelog-lecture/past-prelog-lecturers-and-their-laudations.html|access-date=20 February 2021|website=ETH Zurich|language=en}}</ref> In the same year, she was the president of the Bürgenstock Conference—the Swiss Chemical Society conference on stereochemistry<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bürgenstock Conferences since 1965|url=https://bc18.chemistrycongresses.ch/former-conferences|access-date=20 February 2021|website=bc18.chemistrycongresses.ch}}</ref>—and was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=17 June 2019|title=New Fellows of the Royal Society: V. Gouverneur and J. W. Szostak / Emanuel Merck Lectureship: S. Kitagawa|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.201905609|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|language=en|volume=58|issue=25|pages=8277|doi=10.1002/anie.201905609|pmid=31106954|bibcode=2019ACIE...58.8277. |s2cid=195661180 |issn=1433-7851|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2021, she was awarded the Henri Moissan International Prize for her work in fluorine chemistry. In 2022, she received the [[Arthur C. Cope Award]] conferred by the [[American Chemical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Recipients |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding/awards/national/recipients/2022-recipients.html |access-date=2 November 2022 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref> and was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Members |url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2022 |access-date=2 November 2022 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, she also received the [[European Chemical Society]]'s award for Female Organic Chemist of the Year.<ref name="Merton College, Oxford-2022" /> 

In 2024 Gouverneur was awarded  Royal Society [[The Davy Medal]] for contributions to the field of fluorine chemistry with applications in both medicine and positron emission tomography imaging.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Gouverneur wins Royal Society Award |url=https://www.magd.ox.ac.uk/news/professor-gouverneur-wins-royal-society-award/ |access-date=16 December 2024 |website=Magdalen College |language=en-US}}</ref>
